title: Memory T Follicular Helper CD4 T Cells
summary: Review defining the memory Tfh compartment. Establishes core Tfh markers (CXCR5, BCL6) and the concept that Tfh-committed CD4 T cells persist at the memory stage and recall Tfh effector functions on reactivation. Markers CXCR5 and Bcl6 here are described at the phenotype/transcription-factor level; in the King et al. atlas the corresponding evidence is transcriptomic (CXCR5, BCL6 transcripts).
quotes: T follicular helper (Tfh) cells are the subset of CD4 T helper cells that are required for generation and maintenance of germinal center reactions and the generation of long-lived humoral immunity.

Tfh cells are characterized by their expression of the chemokine receptor CXCR5, expression of the transcriptional repressor Bcl6, and their capacity to migrate to the follicle and promote germinal center B cell responses.

The implication of these findings is that memory Tfh cells retain their capacity to recall their Tfh-specific effector functions upon reactivation to provide help for B cell responses and play an important role in prime and boost vaccination or during recall responses to infection.

title: Cxc Chemokine Receptor 5 Expression Defines Follicular Homing T Cells with B Cell Helper Function
summary: Foundational study identifying CXCR5+ follicular-homing T cells in human tonsil. Reports that tonsillar memory (not naive) CD4 T cells are overwhelmingly CXCR5+ and express activation/costimulatory markers CD69, HLA-DR and ICOS, while downregulating CCR7 and CD62L consistent with follicular residence. All markers here are surface-protein / flow-cytometry measurements.
quotes: Memory but not naive T cells from tonsils are CXCR5+ and migrate in response to the B cell–attracting chemokine 1 (BCA-1), which is selectively expressed by reticular cells and blood vessels within B cell follicles.

title: CD4+ T Follicular Helper Cells in Human Tonsils and Blood Are Clonally Convergent but Divergent from Non-Tfh CD4+ Cells
summary: Matched human tonsil and blood study comparing circulating Tfh and tonsillar Tfh within the CD4+ memory (CD45RA-negative) compartment, using the surface Tfh markers CXCR5, PD-1 and ICOS. Confirms that human tonsillar Tfh are defined within antigen-experienced/memory CD4 T cells. Markers are protein/flow-cytometry level.
quotes: We refer to all antigen-experienced (CD4 + CD45RA − ) cells as memory cells, although this definition encompasses central memory and effector memory/effector T cells, which we did not distinguish in this study.

title: Human Extrafollicular CD4+ T Helper Cells Help Memory B Cells Produce Immunoglobulins
summary: Characterises human tonsillar CD4+ T cell subsets sharing the Tfh phenotype. Documents the canonical Tfh signature of CXCR5, PD-1, IL-21 secretion and BCL6, and contrasts follicle/germinal-centre-localised Tfh with an extrafollicular subset. Markers CXCR5, PD-1 and BCL6 here are protein/flow-cytometry and transcription-factor measurements.

title: Follicular B Helper T Cells Express Cxc Chemokine Receptor 5, Localize to B Cell Follicles, and Support Immunoglobulin Production
summary: Demonstrates the B-cell helper function of tonsillar CXCR5+ memory (CD45RO+) CD4 T cells: co-culture with autologous B cells drives a large increase in immunoglobulin (IgA, IgG) production compared with the CXCR5- fraction. Markers CXCR5 and CD45RO are surface-protein / flow-sorting measurements.

title: Interconnected subsets of memory follicular helper T cells have different effector functions
summary: Defines memory Tfh heterogeneity: local (lymphoid-organ-resident) and circulating memory Tfh subsets that both sustain B-cell responses on reactivation, but with distinct effector outcomes (local cells favour plasma-cell differentiation, circulating cells favour secondary germinal centres). Functional/localisation evidence.
quotes: Memory follicular helper T cells can be local in draining lymphoid organs and circulate in the blood, but the underlying mechanisms of this subdivision are unresolved.

Here we show that both memory follicular helper T subsets sustain B-cell responses after reactivation. Local cells promote more plasma cell differentiation, whereas circulating cells promote more secondary germinal centers.

title: Vaccination establishes clonal relatives of germinal center T cells in the blood of humans
summary: Human study of germinal-centre Tfh in paired tonsil and blood samples. Provides the surface-phenotype benchmark (high CXCR5, PD1, ICOS, plus the transcription factor BCL6) against which the tonsillar memory Tfh compartment is defined. Cited by paraphrase; no verbatim quote retained.
